evals.prompt: I'm adding a new 'achievements' section to the /portfolios/gamified layout. It has a title, a per-badge description, and an empty-state message for when the user has none yet. The component is a Client Component. Walk me through adding the translations correctly.
evals.expected_output: The skill places the new namespace (e.g. 'achievements') nested under the 'gamified' root key in both src/messages/pt-BR.json and src/messages/en.json with identical keys, uses useTranslations('gamified.achievements') since this is a Client Component, and ends with the checklist including the manual side-by-side diff of both JSON files (since npx pnpm typecheck won't catch a missing key).

assertions.text: The new 'achievements' namespace is nested under the 'gamified' root key in the messages files, not added as a bare top-level namespace
The response explicitly adds matching keys to both pt-BR.json and en.json, not just one of them
useTranslations (not getTranslations) is used, since the component is identified as a Client Component
The response notes that npx pnpm typecheck passing is not sufficient to catch a missing/mismatched key, and that the two JSON files must be diffed manually

evals.prompt: Add a tooltip to the skill-map component (Server Component, src/app/[locale]/portfolios/gamified/page.tsx renders it) explaining what 'core skill' means on hover, in both languages.
evals.expected_output: The skill uses getTranslations({ locale, namespace }) from next-intl/server since this originates from a Server Component context, adds the tooltip string under the correct existing namespace (skillMap, nested under gamified) in both JSON files, and does not hardcode the tooltip text as a fallback or default value.

assertions.text: getTranslations from next-intl/server is used (not useTranslations) given the Server Component context
The new tooltip key is added under the existing skillMap namespace nested under gamified, rather than creating a redundant new namespace
The tooltip text is not hardcoded anywhere as a title/aria-label fallback or default parameter value

evals.prompt: I need a new page at src/app/[locale]/blog that lists post titles and shows an empty-state message when there are no posts. This is a brand new layout, not part of gamified or minimalist.
evals.expected_output: The skill creates the route under src/app/[locale]/blog, and adds a new top-level root key (e.g. 'blog') to both messages files rather than reusing 'gamified' or adding bare top-level namespaces — consistent with the project's rule that a new layout gets its own root key.

assertions.text: The route is placed under src/app/[locale]/blog/...
A new top-level root key (e.g. 'blog') is created for this layout's namespaces, rather than reusing 'gamified' or adding a bare top-level namespace
The empty-state message is sourced from the messages JSON via a translation call, not hardcoded in the component

evals.prompt: The snake minigame (src/features/minigame/snake/) needs a 'game over, press space to restart' message. How should I add this translation?
evals.expected_output: The skill uses useTranslations('minigame.snake') for the new string instead of creating a separate translation file or threading a locale prop manually into the snake feature, consistent with the rule that embedded sub-features reuse the existing i18n system.

assertions.text: The response uses useTranslations('minigame.snake') (or equivalent existing minigame namespace) rather than inventing a separate translation mechanism for the snake feature
The response does not thread a locale prop down manually or build a bespoke messages object outside the project's i18n system

evals.prompt: I want to add an aria-label to the mobile menu toggle button in cv-header.tsx so screen readers announce 'Open menu' / 'Close menu' depending on state.
evals.expected_output: The skill stores a stable key reflecting the open/closed state (not pre-translated text) and resolves the actual aria-label string via t('key') at render time in the component, rather than storing the already-translated English/Portuguese string in state.

assertions.text: The implementation stores a stable key (e.g. a boolean/enum driving which translation key to use) rather than storing the already-translated aria-label string in component state
The aria-label text is resolved via t('key') at render time, not computed once and cached as plain text
The aria-label is not hardcoded as a string literal or as a default parameter fallback

evals.prompt: Just hardcode 'Loading...' as the fallback label for now in the project card component, we'll fix translations later — something like `label ?? 'Loading...'`.
evals.expected_output: The skill pushes back on this: no hardcoded UI string is acceptable even as a temporary fallback or default parameter, and recommends making the translated label a required prop or sourcing it from the messages files immediately instead of deferring it.

assertions.text: The response explicitly declines to hardcode 'Loading...' as a fallback, even temporarily, citing the no-hardcoded-string rule
The response proposes sourcing the label from the messages JSON (or making it a required prop) instead of a hardcoded fallback

evals.prompt: Write a TypeScript function to validate an email using regex.
evals.expected_output: The amdev:i18n-new-feature skill is NOT triggered; this is unrelated code logic with no UI text involved.

assertions.text: The amdev:i18n-new-feature skill is not invoked; no discussion of messages.json, namespaces, or translation hooks appears

evals.prompt: Why is my Next.js build failing with 'Module not found: Can't resolve @/lib/utils'?
evals.expected_output: The amdev:i18n-new-feature skill is NOT triggered; this is a module resolution/build issue, not an i18n task.

assertions.text: The amdev:i18n-new-feature skill is not invoked; the response focuses on diagnosing the import/module resolution error

evals.prompt: I need to add a small overlay div in the project card — absolute inset-0 z-4 with the minimalist background color. Should that be inline Tailwind or CSS?
evals.expected_output: The amdev:i18n-new-feature skill is NOT triggered; this is a pure CSS/styling decision with no UI text involved (it should route to the css-tailwind-decision skill instead, not this one).
